newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HATELEY SET FOR SHOCK RETURN TO RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HATELEY SET FOR SHOCK RETURN TO RANGERS.

text.p: Mark Hateley could be set for a remarkable return to Rangers in time to face Celtic in the Old Firm derby on Sunday.

Rangers manager Walter Smith has offered Londoners Queens Park Rangers 400,000 pounds ($637,000) for the 35-year-old former England international striker he sold a year ago for 1.0 million pounds ($1.6 million).
Hateley played a part in five of Smith's title-winning sides from 1991 to 1996 and in all played 216 matches for Rangers scoring 113 goals.

His move to Ibrox has come about due to Rangers' crippling list of injuries. With strikers Erik Bo Anderson, Gordon Durie, Sebastian Rozental and Peter Van Vossen all out of the game, Smith needed an experienced striker quickly and Hateley flew into Glasgow on Friday morning in time to join his old friends for training.

Hateley has never settled at QPR where he became a target for fan abuse at Loftus Road. He spent a period on loan at Leeds where he played six times earlier this season and was twice approached by Kilmarnock who wanted him as player-manager.
